summary: The stones of the priest’s breastpiece stand in ordered rows. The feminine noun can designate a camp of tents or a built enclosure.

senses.definition: The stones on the breastpiece are mounted in four rows. Courses of stone and timber make up the courtyard wall.
The princes of Ishmael have settlements and encampments. The psalm asks for the camp to fall empty, with nobody left in its tents. Peter quotes this prayer when the disciples consider Judas’s place.
The brothers imagine building a silver battlement on a wall. In Ezekiel a course of masonry surrounds the court above its cooking places.

note: How the camp sense arose from the same consonants as a row remains uncertain. The Biblical Aramaic טוּר “mountain” is supported under tsur (xi.aa.ad) and has a distinct sense. Jetur’s genealogy gives no interpretation of his name.
